item.title: ci: relieve the macOS queue
item.body:
Not a lot: CI change, operator go (2026-10-27) to remove CI bottlenecks within our rights.

**Problem.** The macOS runners (`xcode-27`, `macos-26`) are saturated: jobs wait for tens of minutes and `Analyze (swift)` repeatedly fails with "The job was not acquired by Runner … capacity constraints". The ruleset requires branches to be up to date, so every merge re-runs full CI on the next PR.

**Change.**
- `ci.yml`: `HFRKit tests (macOS) + iOS 27 build` now needs the existing change-detection job and runs only when the PR touches `Packages/` or `ci.yml` (pushes to dev-swift always run it). A job skipped by `if:` reports "skipped", which satisfies the required check — the same mechanism the CodeQL Swift gate already relies on (CONTRIBUTING §2). Claim and docs PRs stop using a macOS runner.
- `codeql.yml`: `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress` for pull requests only (group by ref); pushes to dev-swift and the schedule are grouped by SHA and never cancelled, so post-merge analysis always completes.
- CONTRIBUTING §2 table updated.

Not changed (owner's settings, asked to ezzz separately): the up-to-date requirement, auto-merge, required checks.

**Checks.** actionlint (v1.7.7) clean apart from the pre-existing custom runner labels; markdownlint clean. This PR touches `ci.yml`, so its own engine job runs.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * macOS engine and app checks run when relevant files change or change detection fails; otherwise, pull requests can skip them. Swift analysis also runs when Swift changes are detected or change detection fails.
  * Pull request runs are grouped by pull request and can cancel earlier runs. Other runs are grouped separately and are not cancelled.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated merge criteria to clarify when macOS tests, iOS builds, and Swift analysis are skipped or run.

@@ -9,9 +9,10 @@ on:
 permissions:
   contents: read
 
+# A new push to a PR cancels its running CI; pushes to dev-swift are never cancelled.
 concurrency:
-  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
-  cancel-in-progress: true
+  group: ci-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.sha }}
review_comments.body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Use a unique group for non-PR runs.** When a push and manual dispatch target the same commit, both runs enter `ci-`. If a third run enters that group while one runs and one waits, GitHub cancels the pending run despite `cancel-in-progress: false`. Use `github.run_id` for non-PR runs so a requested CI run is not discarded. The same SHA grouping appears in `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` at Line 16. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency?utm_source=openai))
Proposed CI change
```diff --- "a/.github/workflows/ci.yml" +++ "b/.github/workflows/ci.yml" @@ -11,7 +11,7 @@ # A new push to a PR cancels its running CI; pushes to dev-swift are never cancelled. concurrency: - group: ci-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.sha }} + group: ci-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.run_id }} cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} jobs: ```
Committable suggestion
> **IMPORTANT** > Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements. ```suggestion group: ci-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.run_id }} ```

After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

review_comments.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Make change-detection failures block the required checks.** `engine-apple` and `Analyze (swift)` depend on `Detect app changes` and `Detect Swift changes`. If either detector fails, GitHub skips the dependent job, and skipped required jobs report success. The ruleset requires the gated checks but not either detector, so a failed detector can let a PR merge without the corresponding validation. Require both detector jobs, or make each dependent job fail when detection fails, then update this documentation. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ezzz/HFRnow/e30fcb09f65fb9605d83fa41a5d0283663c543ee/.github/workflows/ci.yml))
